title: KV lattice memory weave for tensor/pipeline parallel coordination
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: As we push continuous batching on mixed tensor/pipeline parallel jobs, existing slab/stripe approaches cause hotspots and frequent cross-device stalls when large KV entries are retrieved. This ticket proposes a KV lattice (memory weave) coordinator that (1) maps KV slabs into a logical lattice overlay aligned to both tensor and pipeline dimensions, (2) maintains lightweight liveness bands for hot prefixes, and (3) drives a prioritized prefetch + spill plan that minimizes cross-stage stalls while bounding additional memory overhead. Goals: reduce stall-related tail latency by >=20% on TP+PP workloads, keep extra cross-GPU bandwidth <15% average, and reduce required spare host memory for spilling compared to baseline by 30%.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by infra and runtime leads
End-to-end prototype integrated with runtime prefetch hook and KV manager
Benchmarks: 95th percentile token latency improved >=20% versus current slab-striping baseline for mixed TP+PP models (e.g., 8TPx2PP config)
Memory overhead of lattice planning <12% of total GPU KV allocation for steady-state workload
Fallback policy: if coordinator fails, system reverts to existing contiguous-slab placement without correctness impact
tasks: Add prefetch policy and liveness tracker to KV manager
Integrate with runtime scheduling hook for pipeline stage placement
Create benchmark harness for mixed TP/PP microbenchmarks
Run experiments across instance types (A100, H100) and record metrics
Add e2e tests for correctness and graceful fallback
Open PR and collect reviews from runtime, scheduling, and perf teams
decisions: Use a 2D logical lattice keyed by (tensor-block-id, pipeline-stage-id) rather than per-GPU fixed stripes to allow flexible remapping for heterogeneous topologies
Prefetch policy will be asymmetric: aggressive for hot prefixes with small tokens, conservative for large KV entries to avoid bandwidth spikes
Eviction uses age+hotness banding; eviction must consider downstream pipeline stage affinity to avoid immediate re-prefetches
tradeoffs: Lattice planning adds CPU overhead each rebalancing epoch (~5-10ms per node in initial prototype) vs. static striping which has near-zero planner cost
Prefetch reduces stalls but increases cross-GPU bandwidth; chosen conservative thresholds aim to keep bandwidth increase under 15% on average
More aggressive replication of hot slabs reduces latency but increases memory footprint and complicates consistency during model rollouts
benchmarks: Prototype run: GPT-3.5-like 8TPx2PP workload: baseline 95p token latency 110ms -> lattice prototype 85ms (22.7% improvement)
Cross-GPU bandwidth measured increase: +11% average, +28% short spike during warmup (controlled by backoff)
Spill-to-host usage: baseline peak 42GB -> lattice plan peak 29GB (31% reduction) on 8xA100 topology
